traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.55, 0.53, 0.48], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

appearance.twig.note: Sargent's Manual (2nd ed. 1922, read at the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18), as Ficus aurea, p. 334: "terete pithy light orange-colored branchlets marked by pale lenticels". Colour chosen by eye for light orange.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Sargent's Manual (2nd ed. 1922, read at the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18), as Ficus aurea, p. 334: "Leaves oblong ... 2'-5' long, 1½'-3' wide, thick and coriaceous ... petioles stout, slightly grooved, ½'-1' in length".

generator.params.bloom_area.note: The leaf area its `bloom` look draws on an organ 1 m long (visual forms Skill 1, 2026-10-14; plantc atlas), so it shades with what it shows: the look now takes its card from the taxa's characters, where before it drew the generic card (-).

traits.height_max_m.note: Sargent's Manual (2nd ed. 1922), as Ficus aurea: a broad round-topped tree, starting as an epiphyte, 50 to 60 ft high (15.2 m to 18.3 m). Small's Manual of the Southeastern Flora (1933, p. 439) says a shrub, or a tree becoming 20 m tall.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Ficus aurea (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.45 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 4 records in 4 sources); trunks 0.45, branches 0.46. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region. Refitted 2026-10-18 from 16.1 to 8.87 when its leaves became single true-size leaves from Sargent's measures: the fuller crown gathered more vigour and grew 18.0 m at 80 years against its 14 m reference; now 14.0 m.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: an evergreen fig of southern Florida, 10 to 20 m tall, that often starts as a seedling high in another tree and sends roots down round it; its broad crown drops aerial roots that thicken into pillars where they reach the ground, over a buttressed base and long surface roots; leathery, glossy oval leaves. Not fitted to measurements. Its crown's width is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured width over height of open-grown trees of its lineage (crown_spread, USDA Urban Tree Database) since 2026-10-23, in place of a hand-set crown_radius.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 9 m at 25 years and 14 m at 80; this proxy grows from the ground. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: dark glossy leaves, smooth pale grey bark. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): smooth light grey bark; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2809576), as no source read gives it.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Sargent's Manual (2nd ed. 1922, read at the Internet Archive, 2026-10-18), as Ficus aurea, p. 334: "Leaves oblong ... 2'-5' long, 1½'-3' wide, thick and coriaceous ... petioles stout, slightly grooved, ½'-1' in length".
